skill_evidence_map.caveat: snr = sqrt(rms^2 - floor^2)/floor per group. The median group is below snr 1 at every dose in all three 24 h lines, so most of this benchmark is below its own measurement error; a 24-dim mechanism-class one-hot matches a 2048-bit fingerprint across 4 datasets x 4 learned models. The matched test shows dose predicts model skill only through measurability in the 24 h lines (attenuation 96-144%, conditional CI straddling zero) but NOT at 72 h, where the assay already clears its floor. A Dynamic Range Fraction against an interpolated duplicate -- a calibrated metric that is not ours -- agrees, and more strongly: the dynamic range is negative at low dose and low snr, so even a reliability-shrunk technical duplicate cannot beat the dose-mean baseline.

skill_evidence_map.caveat: Independent platform, lab and scale: 1,750 compounds over 9 cell lines at a median of 3 replicates. The median condition has snr 0.000 and 74% have exactly zero noise-corrected signal, so the measurability result is not a property of sci-Plex; it holds more strongly here, which makes the sci-Plex figures the optimistic ones.

Trained from scratch on our split, since the released checkpoints would leak held-out compounds. Over five paired split seeds it is statistically indistinguishable from the Tanimoto-kernel ridge: mean margin +0.0029 in the kernel ridge's favour, bootstrap 95% CI [-0.0019, +0.0077], chemCPA ahead on 1 of 5 seeds. The single-seed 0.0055 advantage, and its apparent concentration in the top snr quartile, were both properties of split 42 -- the q4 margin flips sign in 3 of 5 seeds. The same model ranges 0.1016-0.1247 across seeds from the held-out set alone, which is larger than the gap between models, and is the measurability result appearing in a model comparison.
Asks whether the response model generalises or recognises mechanism classes; the reference arm must reproduce the headline result before any arm is interpreted.

open_limitations: Four datasets are now analysed (A549 24 h and 72 h, K562 24 h, MCF7 24 h), but the models are fitted and compared within a dataset; no cross-cell-line transfer model is trained.
The 72 h arm covers one cell line and a 47-compound subset enriched for HDAC and Aurora, so the time comparison is run on compounds matched to the 24 h panel.
Pseudobulk group means only; single-cell distributions and dose-response shape are not modelled.
Two replicates per compound/dose, so the replicate noise floor is itself imprecise; the measurability conclusions rest on medians over 183-188 groups per dose, not on single groups.
The replicate floor scales as ~1/sqrt(cells), so "low dose is unmeasurable" is a statement about this assay depth, not evidence that low-dose responses are biologically absent.

chemCPA vs our kernel ridge is not resolved by this benchmark: over 5 paired seeds the margin is +0.0029 with a 95% CI of [-0.0019, +0.0077]. Split-to-split variation (same model, 0.1016-0.1247) exceeds the between-model difference, so no ranking is supportable. chemCPA also ran at its shipped hyperparameters; a tuned configuration was not tried.
Cytotoxic compounds lose cells at QC; their responses describe surviving cells.
Docking is rigid-receptor with no explicit zinc chemistry; AutoDock4Zn needs autogrid4, not installed.
ESOL property model uses one seeded split; no uncertainty estimate.
No claim of disease rescue, direct binding, or efficacy is made anywhere in these outputs.
